utterances.text: Did you stop anywhere before Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes. At a location after Kravica. I think it's called Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was going on there that made you stop?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: There were some Muslim forces that had surrendered. General Mladic stopped there and addressed them. He gave a speech. He told them that as the people, they were not to blame, that the authorities, their commanders and presidents, were to blame. He asked them where they wished to go, to which territory. He requested that buses be provided and that they be transported to the territory where they wished to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay there in the area of the Sandici village, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't think it was long, 20 minutes at most, but I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Chamber how many prisoners were there, in your estimate?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I think perhaps 3- or 400 people, but I can't know. I did not count them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As for those people, were they secured?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the people who were guarding the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In which direction did you move after this?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: We moved in the direction of Konjevic Polje and Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we go, can I just ask one clarification, sir. Sir, did the buses that General Mladic ordered arrive while you were still there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please tell the Chamber where you stopped next.

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: The next stop was at a location called Kasaba, before Milici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber in more detail what sort of location it was where you stopped.

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: It's a place before Milici - I think it was a football pitch - and that was where we stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What happened after you stopped there?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: General Mladic also addressed those. There was a similar number of those who were taken prisoner. He gave them the same speech, a similar one to the one he had given in Sandici. That was how he addressed these people too. From there, we continued on towards Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether you were able to hear what General Mladic said at the football pitch in Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Well, he told them that they had been betrayed, that their commander Naser Oric had sold them, betrayed them, something along those lines, that as people they were not guilty at all, that politics pursued by their president were to blame. I don't remember anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice if anyone was abused or mistreated or if any of the prisoners were beaten?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't notice, and nothing like that took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In your estimate, how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: It was a very short stop; up to 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please tell the Chamber in which direction you continued your journey and how far did you go?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: In the direction of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you stop in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you stop and where were you personally?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: We were in front of a building. I think it was some command. We went there to have lunch. And we waited for General Mladic there, in front of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, how long did you stay in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Oh, I can't remember. Maybe an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In what vehicle did you escort the vehicle that General Mladic was in, on that day?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: It was a Pinzgauer vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what General Mladic did in this building in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it a military building?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: We moved on, towards Han Pijesak, and we were providing escort.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How far did you escort General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: We escorted him to the gas station at the entrance to the town of Han Pijesak itself, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And what happened there?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: He stopped there to refuel his vehicle and ours. He said good-bye to us and ordered us to return to the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you do so?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, when did you return to the brigade command that evening?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but it was during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, during this trip from Bratunac via Sandici, Konjevic Polje, Kasaba, and Vlasenica, did you at any moment while stopping notice Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you at any moment during the trip hear from someone else from the escort that General Mladic met Momir Nikolic on that day along this route?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, please tell us, to the best of your recollection, when you passed by the football pitch in Kasaba on your way back, could you notice whether there were any prisoners there still?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you passed by Sandici, or rather through Sandici during that evening, do you remember whether the prisoners were still in the same location which you have described when you were moving towards Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Before the witness's answer, again in the revised summary there's no detailed information about his observations on the return to Bratunac. There's no information directing me as to what could potentially come out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that's correct. But it's a summary, and I think that this question is substantial and very detailed. There are other issues that are not included in the summary that we have provided. I don't see what's disputable about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, what is disputable is not that the question is not detailed but the issue is whether in your 65 ter summary you covered the subjects you would ask the witness about, and Mr. Gillett, I think, refers to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And if I may, the only sentence even vaguely referring to this is where it says -- it's the second-last paragraph of the summary. It says: "After the meeting that General Mladic had in command in Vlasenica, they continued the General's escort to Han Pijesak where they stopped, poured fuel, and then by the General's orders went back in Bratunac." Then it goes on to the witness's comments about Momir Nikolic. So there's simply no indication of facts that could come from this witness on which we could prepare for the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You are -- it is hereby on the record. If it will have any further consequences as far as your preparation is concerned, Mr. Gillett, then, of course, we'll ... Mr. Stojanovic, you're giving the impression that you consider it not that relevant. The Chamber considers this to be relevant. But for the time being, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will finish with one additional question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, that evening, upon arrival to Bratunac, did you submit a report to anyone, you or any of the other members of the military police group? I mean, did you report about discharging the task that you carried out on that day?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I didn't, and I don't know about the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, thank you for answering my questions. At this point we have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Andric, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Gillett. You find him to your right. Mr. Gillett is counsel for the Prosecution. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Andric. I'm going ask you a few questions.

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If any of them are unclear, please let me know and I'll do my best to revise them. Firstly, you mentioned in direct testimony stopping at Sandici during the escort mission with Mladic; correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You've previously given statements to the authorities in Bosnia; correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could we get 65 ter document 32386 on the monitor. And if we go to page 1. For this document, the pages in B/C/S and English should be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, if we look at page 1, we see the date of this statement is 29 June 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, these documents were recently received from the BiH authorities. One being as we understand the original in B/C/S, and a translation by the BH authorities in English. And where there are slight discrepancies between the original and the translation, I'll endeavour to address those with the witness where relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, as you suggest.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now we see under the title "attendees," that the prosecutor is Kwai Hong Ip and several other people are present at the interview. And we see in the B/C/S version, the original, at the top that the word "Sarajevo" is crossed out and "Tuzla" is written there. Does this indicate that the interview took place in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Well, interviews were conducted both in Sarajevo and in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Do you recollect whether this interview was conducted in Tuzla as it appears to indicate on the B/C/S original?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't confirm that. I know that I gave a statement in Sarajevo and also another one in Tuzla. That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we could go to page 6 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: We see your signature with the names -- with the words "svedok" underneath. Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You told the truth during this interview, correct, that we're seeing on the monitor?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, in the statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And if we could go to paragraph 2 which is on page 3 --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: -- you describe in the statement events in Sandici during the escort mission with General Mladic. And I'm going to read to you what you state. This is at paragraph 2. It states: "On 13 July 1995, when I was on the Sandici meadow, General Mladic talked to the prisoners who were collected there. In that area I saw between 400 and 500 men. I heard Mladic telling these prisoners that he would provide buses for them to go where they wished. I got the impression that this speech as well as the circumstances had been staged because the buses appeared almost at the same time. As soon as the buses arrived, I heard Mladic shouting, 'All of you get in the bus!' About two to three buses arrived. I did not notice either journalists, TV cameras, or reporters in the Sandici meadow." Sir, do you stand by that statement in paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, if you could explain? A few moments ago, you were asked by Judge Moloto whether the buses arrived at Sandici meadow while you were present, and this is at temporary transcript page 49, your response was: No. Can you explain this discrepancy?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I can explain that a lot of time passed -- passed since, and at this point in time, right now, I cannot remember every detail to say whether they had arrived or not. Perhaps at the moment when I gave this statement, I remembered that they had arrived. But now, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And your recollection was better in 2006 than it is today in 2015; correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to refer to some other paragraphs of this statement. I wonder if I could tender it to get an exhibit number now so that we have a consistent number throughout the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll reserve a number for it, and do you want to tender the whole of the statement after that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We could already reserve a number. And then after you've dealt with all the portions, there will be an opportunity to raise any objections against admission. Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number reserved for document would be P7295, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll later decide on admission. But before we continue. Witness, when Judge Moloto earlier asked you whether the buses that General Mladic ordered arrived while you were still there, your answer was no. I now understand that your answer is: I don't remember whether they did or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you be very precise in telling us exactly what you do not remember or whether you have a clear recollection what happened. Because here we might have been misled by you answering that those buses did not arrive, whereas we now understand you just don't remember whether they arrived when you were still there. Could you please keep that in mind when answering any further questions. Please proceed, Mr. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we look at paragraph 3, the first few sentences read the following: "After Mladic's speaking to the prisoners, I received the information from one of my colleagues, I do not remember from whom, that General Mladic spoke to some commanders who were on the Sandici meadow. I saw General Mladic speaking so some officers. I assumed they were commanders because Mladic would never speak to anyone of the lower rank. These officers were wearing two to three different types of uniforms. It is difficult to say, but some of them were wearing blue one-piece uniforms. Perhaps they were the special police." So if I understand this correctly, you saw Mladic speaking to some officers at Sandici meadow; correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't remember precisely at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I'm trying to understand the statement in front of me. It indicates to me that you said that you saw the officers that Mladic was speaking to and that you thought they were commanders because Mladic would -- would not speak to people of a low rank. Could you help us? Is that a way of understanding what is in your statement?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: It is possible, but I don't remember any particular details.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, could we get 65 ter number 32390 on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before this document moves off, did you know any of the officers that Mr. Mladic was talking to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could get 65 ter document which should be a photo, 32390.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And if we look at the ERN in the corner, this is the same ERN that is indicated in a lower portion of the statement that we were just looking at. Now, the soldiers that you saw at Sandici were wearing uniforms like this, some of them; correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: There were different types of uniform. I don't know exactly what kind of uniform they wore.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Were some of them wearing uniforms that looked like the uniforms in this picture?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't remember precisely. I think so. Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: The one closest to the camera in the foreground, do you recall him being present at Sandici meadow?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could we go back to the statement, which is now with exhibit number P7295, temporarily assigned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What would you like to do with the photograph shown to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I was just going to first go to the paragraph of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Again, looking at paragraph 3, if we see the third-last sentence, it says -- I believe it's the third- or fourth-last sentence: "I was shown the photo number 0216-4758. These are the types of uniforms which men who were on the Sandici meadow wore. Most of the Bratunac Brigade members did not have such uniforms." Does that refresh your recollection, that you saw people wearing the types of uniforms in the picture that we've just seen at Sandici meadow?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: There were different kinds of uniform. In all likelihood, there were such uniforms as the ones you are showing me on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Well, sir, standing here now, is it correct or is it not correct what is written in your statement in front of us, that there were people wearing these types of uniforms at Sandici meadow?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I think there were some such uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tendered 65 ter document, this picture, 32390.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 32390 receives number P7296, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I just note for the record that another photograph referred to in that paragraph under the number 0217-4734 [sic] on our understanding according to the ERN is already admitted as P1148 at page 120.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, I'm going to ask you a few questions about the continuation of your escort mission with Mladic now. Now, you said at temporary transcript page 49 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: -- that stopping at Sandici the next stop was at Kasaba, at the football field. Do you recall saying that a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could we now go to -- sorry. If we stay with the same statement and turn across the page to paragraph 8, which should be on page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that, Mr. Gillett, the number you referred to on line 19, page 60, starts with 0217, whereas I see all the documents referred in that paragraph started with 0216. Is there any possibility that you misspoke?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, I did misspeak on that. 0216 should be the initial digit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, looking at paragraph 8 of the statement, it reads -- in fact, apologies. If we could go back to paragraph 7 just to provide the context here. If we go back a page. And if we see in paragraph 7, the opening sentence talks about after Mladic leaving Sandici, you following him in a military vehicle. And then if we turn over to paragraph 8, on the next page, it states: "As we were approaching the cross-roads towards Konjevic Polje, I saw that Mladic stopped his vehicle approximately 100 metres before the cross-roads. The vehicle I was in was around 20 to 30 metres away from Mladic's vehicle. I saw that Mladic got out of the vehicle and spoke to a group of 20 soldiers." It then continues. Paragraph 9 refers to a technical matter. And then paragraph 10, the first sentence says: "We stayed in Konjevic Polje for about ten minutes." And then it states: "After leaving Konjevic Polje, we headed to Nova Kasaba and stopped on the football pitch." So, in fact, the next stop on the escort mission was at Konjevic Polje, not Nova Kasaba; correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: We did not get out of the vehicle. He did stop his vehicle and got out, but we stayed inside. We were a part of the column. As for any further details, in terms of how it happened, well, after this much time, I can't recall any.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, my question wasn't about whether you got out of the vehicle. It was about whether the next stop on the escort mission was at Konjevic Polje. And it's true, that was the next stop of the escort mission, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So what you said earlier at temporary transcript page 49 in relation to Konjevic Polje was incorrect, because it omitted the stop at Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know. That's what you think.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Well, I'm not asking for your observations on what I think. I'm asking for an answer to the question. What you said earlier in saying that the next stop after Sandici was Kasaba was incorrect, because there was a stop at Konjevic Polje. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we could now go to page 4, paragraph 12, of the same statement which should still be on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And I understand that after Kasaba, you continued on in the direction of Milici; right?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And here's what you state: "Fifteen minutes later, we started from there to Milici. On the way to Milici, we stopped at the outskirts of Milici. I noticed a man appearing from the woods. He was carrying a stick or a piece of wood in his hand. We were moving fast and we had to stop the car abruptly. We jumped out of the vehicle, and I heard Mladic shouting at him, What are you doing, why aren't you fighting?! Then I saw Mladic ordering," and I understand in B/C/S this says his body-guards, "to slap that man several times. This man was old and I assume that he was a local. This happened 20 to 30 metres in front of me. I saw Mladic ordering this man to take off his underpants to check whether that man was Muslim." Do you stand by what is written here in paragraph 12 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we then look to paragraph 14, we see that after the stop in Vlasenica, you continued on the road and you stopped in front of a building where there was some policemen. And this what is you state in paragraph 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: This is pages 4 through to 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: "We left Vlasenica and headed to Han Pijesak. We stopped in front of a building, I think it was in Han Pogled. I saw 20 to 30 civil policemen sitting. They carried automatic guns. They were young men. I saw Mladic getting out of his vehicle. Then I saw a man who seemed to be the commander of that police unit approaching Mladic. Mladic shouted at this commander saying what are you doing here? You are lying there while other soldiers are getting killed! Why don't you go to the nearby hills and wait there on Muslim forces coming from Srebrenica?! They will find you here and cut your throats. Then Mladic ordered his bodyguard to slap this commander five times. The bodyguard did so and then Mladic started to shout at his bodyguard saying" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should slow down, otherwise it's very complicated to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: "The bodyguard did so and then Mladic started shouting at his body-guard saying slap him five times, and then he said why don't you hit him harder Serb motherfucker. He would otherwise slap him five times. Then the body-guard slapped him another five times. Then the policemen went to the woods." These policemen that you saw were Bosnian Serb policemen; right?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And when you say that Mladic told the body-guard to hit the commander harder and that he would do it otherwise, that means Mladic would slap the commander if the body-guard didn't slap him. Is that the correct understanding of what you state?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know what he thought. That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I'm interested in what he said. In what he said, did Mladic mean that if the body-guard did not slap him harder, that Mladic would slap him harder? Is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't think it was Mladic who would slap the man. I think it would be Mladic slapping the body-guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for clarifying that. And you stand by this paragraph of your statement; right?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now you continue to state that after seeing the policemen in Han Pogled, Mladic went to the main road and stopped traffic. And I'm moving to paragraph 15 here of the statement, which reads: "After this, Mladic went to the main road and stopped the traffic which was flowing there. I cannot remember how many vehicles he stopped, but those were Serb civilians. One of the vehicles was returning from the funeral, and people in that vehicle were dressed in black. A woman was crying and Mladic told her, I don't care about the funeral. It makes no sense to cry. Go to the woods, pick a stone or a piece of wood, and kill Turks. Then he told all people who got out of the car which included women, too, shouting at them, Go to the woods, pick a piece of wood or a stick, go to the hills, and try to ambush Muslims coming from Srebrenica. I cannot recall if he called these Muslims from Srebrenica Muslims or Turks. However, he must probably said Turks. Serb civilians were surprised but nevertheless they went to the woods." Sir, the main road you're referring to is the road between Vlasenica and Han Pijesak; right?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And when Mladic said to the crying women, "I don't care about the funeral. It makes no sense to cry. Go to the woods, pick a stone or a piece of wood, and kill Turks," how were you able to hear that?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I could hear it because I was very close and he spoke loudly. But I don't think he said so word for word. He said something to the effect that the Turks should be stopped in their passage. It is possible that I phrased it the way it is in the statement at the time, but I don't remember any specific details right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, by "Turks," Mladic was referring to Bosnian Muslims; correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And this was quite a memorable event stopping the funeral vehicle; correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You've already told us that your recollection was better in 2006 when this statement was taken, so in fact it's correct that he said to the crying women, "I don't care about the funeral. It makes no sense to cry. Go to the woods, pick a stone or a piece of wood, and kill Turks," that's correct as written in your signed statement, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: It is possible that it is how it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: My -- sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No -- no audible speaking. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you a few questions about a different topic, which is events at the -- I see Your Honour has an intervention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, I just wanted to take a look at paragraph 20 of this document, and I just wanted to find out from the witness -- Sir, you're mentioning a number of people who were with you on the 13th of July on this Pinzgauer. One of them is Mitrovic. Can you remember his first name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mitrovic? I think his first name was Milovan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And do you remember the first name of Jakovljevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Boro.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then do you remember the surname of Bosko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you remember the first name of Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember who else was there. I do remember that Mitrovic was there and Jakovljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In this, paragraph you are saying, let me read it to you: "I'm not sure who was in the Pinzgauer with me on the 13th of July 1995 except for Mitrovic and Jakovljevic, whom I have mentioned. However, it may include Bosko, perhaps Nikolic, and Nenad Jokic." Do you remember Nenad Jokic being there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But do you remember Bosko's surname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you remember Nikolic's first name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't. I haven't seen most of them in 20 years. I only see Boro Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps in order to avoid whatever confusion. Irrespective of whether you remember that Nikolic was there, you apparently had on your mind a certain person by the name of Nikolic. Do you remember his first name? So even if he wasn't there, what the first name of Nikolic is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. Perhaps if I had a list of military policemen, I might be able to tell you who there was with the last name of Nikolic. But off the cuff, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do I understand then that you saw mainly military policemen there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that Nikolic, irrespective of whether he was there, that you knew him as a military policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know there was a Nikolic whose first name I don't recall who was a member of the military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's the one had you on your mind when you said that perhaps he may have been there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed -- no. Let's take a break first. That's better. Witness, we'll take a break, and we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes from now. And Mr. Mladic should not speak aloud. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at 1.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I briefly address the Prosecution. There is a renewed request for a witness to be heard through videolink. I think it was a -- a witness for whom a videolink was denied earlier. Kelecevic. Yes. When could the Prosecutor -- Prosecution respond to that request?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Probably within about one minute. I'm virtually certain I know the answer. Let me confirm with an e-mail, and I can certainly get back to the Court before the end of the session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because the organising and scheduling videolinks is not one of the easiest things to do, and the sooner we can start with it the better it would be. It's appreciated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The motion I just referred to was confidential. Therefore, I shouldn't have done that in open session. At the same time, we didn't touch upon any of the content which has caused the confidentiality of that motion. Therefore, there's no need to take any specific measures at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gillett, if you're ready, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, before the break, we were referring to the reference in your statement to a Nikolic. Now, if we could get document -- 65 ter document 46477b if that's -- if we could get 4677, 65 ter document, and go to page 130.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is the number again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It's now correctly recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now what is coming up should be a list of personnel from the Bratunac Brigade, and if we can to page 130, we should see that this is for July 1995 at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, we're just in the process of adding an English translation. But as you'll see, it's essentially a list of names.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could you confirm that this says at the top July 1995?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And if we go across to page 131, so the following page, we see yourself listed Andric, Srecka Pero, with VP, indicating military police; correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Well, do you see it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we enlarge it, the relevant portion?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you. It's about a quarter of the way down the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: On the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Near the top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we see the entire top?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Do you see yourself listed there?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, if we could go to page 149, and near the -- near the top, it's about eight names down, we see a Bosko Nikolic, also listed with VP. Is that possibly the Nikolic that you were referring to in your statement?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I can't see Bosko written here anywhere. Oh, yes. Yes, yes, Nikolic, father's name Vukota.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So it's possible that is the person you were referring to that we were discussing before the break.

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would tender this -- what will become once we've made an excerpt of it, 65 ter document 4677b. And if it's not ready yet, we could deal with that on the close of the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Mr. Stojanovic, any objections? It's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we reserve a number already. The excerpt will be assigned 65 ter number 4677b, and the number to be reserved once it's there and if we decide on admission would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number P7297, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That number is reserved.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, on the evening after your escort mission with Mladic, which I understand to be 13 July, you returned to Bratunac; right?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And once you got to Bratunac, Momir Nikolic ordered the military police of the Bratunac Brigade to go to the Vuk Karadzic school and assist those who were securing the prisoners in that area; right?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Possibly it was so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Are you saying, yes, or no, or you don't recall?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't recall that he ordered personally, but I remember that military police did go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could we get 65 ter document 32391. And Your Honours, while this comes up, this is a transcript of the witness's testimony at the BiH Court, and if we could go to page 12 in English, which is page 13 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And, sir, here you're describing the time when you came back to Bratunac after the escort mission, and you were asked: "And what happens there next, there in front of the command in terms of your group. Were you assigned to any activities, tasks?" And your response: "Well, the group was tasked to go and provide assistance, practically to others who were providing security at or around school in Bratunac. I don't recall the" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gillett, you're reading, and that's where you usually gain too much speed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I'll start this again: "Q. And what happens there next, there in front of the command in terms of your group? Were you assigned to any other activities, tasks? "A. Well, the group was tasked to go on provide assistance, practically to others who were providing security at or around school in Bratunac. I don't recall the exact name but I believe the name is Vuk Karadzic. To my recollection, this order came from Momir Nikolic. He was the one to issue it - the order that we should go and provide assistance to other soldiers and our fellow colleagues who most probably were there in front of the school." Does that refresh your memory as to being ordered by Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we go to page 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You were then asked a follow-up question to clarify. And the second question down, we see in the English - this should be page 30 in B/C/S - is: "Yes, Your Honour, I would ask the witness because it's unclear to me, once he returned from Han Pijesak, the witness told that it was upon the order of Momir Nikolic for the police ... for the military police to go and secure ... and provide security there. From whom did he hear this? "Q. Did you understand this or not?" Response -- and if we can go over the page in B/C/S. "A. To my recollection, Momir Nikolic personally issued this. Who else was in my company, I don't recall. "Q. Hold on a second. Let us clarify. On your return to Bratunac, to the command, from Han Pijesak, did you find Momir Nikolic there? "A. I believe so, yes. "Q. Did you hear that from Momir Nikolic directly? "A. Yes." Sir, you were ordered by Momir Nikolic to go to the Vuk Karadzic school after the escort mission; correct.

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Earlier today --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we ask -- Witness, when you testified in the BiH Court, did you tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do you -- have you any reasons to say that what you told at that time is not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think there is any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do we have the year in which this testimony was given? It's in the introduction. I think you didn't mention it specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: It's on -- it's 2008, according to our understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 2008, yes. Please -- that's at least how you introduce it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, earlier today, you were asked at temporary transcript page 43: "Q. Do you know someone named Momir Nikolic? "A. I do. "Q. What was his duty at the time, his position? "A. As far as I know, he was a security officer in charge of security affairs. "Q. Did you receive specific orders or tasks from him at any point in time? "A. I did not" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic should not speak aloud. It's the last warning, Mr. Mladic. You're removed from the courtroom if it happens again. Let that be clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I'll repeat the question, and this is line 23: "Q. Did you receive specific orders or tasks from him at any point in time? "A. I did not -- I did not but I can't speak for others."

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, in light of what you've just told us, that testimony was incorrect. In fact, you don't remember whether Momir Nikolic gave you orders; right?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't remember anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, you went to the area near the Vuk Karadzic school in Bratunac on the evening of 13 July after the escort mission with Mladic; right?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could we get 65 ter document 32388, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And while that's coming out, you're aware that members of the Bratunac Brigade military police took the Pinzgauer vehicle and parked it in front of the Vuk Karadzic school; right?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, that vehicle was parked in front of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And it was taken there by members of the Bratunac Brigade military police; right?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Probably. I didn't travel in it, but probably they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we look at the statement in front of us, we see it's from 28 February 2007, and again under attendees the prosecutor is Kwai Hong Ip asking questions. Now, if we go to page -- page 7 in the B/C/S original, we can see some photos attached to the statement. These should be colour photographs. And this first photograph at the top shows the street in the centre of Bratunac heading towards the Vuk Karadzic school; right.

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I know the school but not the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Is this the Vuk Karadzic school, to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which, Mr. Gillett?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sorry, let me specify.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Is the light building at the end of the street perpendicular to the road that we can see the school in Bratunac, to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I think so, but I don't know to this day what it's called. I know where it is it located, but there are two or three schools there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Then if we go back to paragraph 4 of your statement, which should be on page 4 of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And again, the English and B/C/S should be the same page numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: At paragraph 4, we see that you state: "I was shown the photograph with PA/1 and I signed and dated it. That is a photograph of Bratunac town centre. I marked with a green marker the locations where the vehicles and trucks were."

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And just for Your Honours, we haven't got to that photo yet, but I'm reading the part of the statement together.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You continue: "I saw those buses and trucks. I heard and saw people in Vuk Karadzic school, but I did not go inside. The windows were open. I also heard that there were other Bosnian Muslims on the stadium and that they were secured there as well as those people in the vehicles. There were many people around the vehicles, soldiers and some of my colleagues. I do not remember who among my colleagues were there. Men of military age were called up to secure vehicles and buildings" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you. And next page in B/C/S, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: It continues: "I noticed young men of 15 and 16 years of age, Serbs who were armed, and who helped securing the area with buses. There were also elderly men who secured the buses. The area with buses was not closed and anyone could approach the buses." Paragraph 5 states: "I was shown photographs PA/1 and PA/3. I signed and dated them. The photograph shows Vuk Karadzic school. At the photograph 4, I drew with a red marker the location of Pinzgauer which I saw when I was in front of the school. There were many people outside the school, minimum 40 people, including my colleagues and other soldiers. I do not remember exactly who was there and I do not remember if anybody was on the Pinzgauer." Now, if we go to page 8 of the B/C/S original, if we go one more page further -- sorry. Sorry, this is the correct page. On the bottom photograph, we can see the red marking made on the photo that you refer to in the earlier part of your statement. That is your indication of where the Pinzgauer was parked; right?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: That is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we go across another page, and if we could zoom in on the area with the green markings made on the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, these are the green markings that you referred to earlier in your statement showing where the buses with the Muslim prisoners were parked that night of 13 July; correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: All this is very unclear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Is that a yes, or a no, or you don't remember?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I'm not familiar with this photograph, and I can't interpret it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we go back to page 6 of this document, we see at the bottom your signature there, don't we? Could you answer my question, sir. Do we see your signature --

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And your recollection in 2007 when this was taken was better than it is now; correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know. How should I know if it was better or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this stage that would conclude my questions, and I would tender the two statements I've been referring to as well as the additional exhibit referring to the Bosko Nikolic. The two statements are 32387, that's the statement I was initially referring to that was given temporary exhibit number P7295. The second statement that we've just been referring to is 32388. And the additional exhibit referring to Bosko Nikolic is 4677b, which is now uploaded in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 32388 receives number P7298, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Then the others, the first statement had received a number already and is admitted into evidence and that was number -- let me just check.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number P7295, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7295 is admitted into evidence. Then 4677b, which is P7297, is admitted into evidence as well. And now we have the other one. Have we reserved a number for that, Madam Registrar, the excerpts still to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sorry, this is the final statement that I was referring to with the photographs attached, which is 65 ter 32388.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And 32391 you're not tendering?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: No, we're not tendering that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then so 65 ter 32388, Madam Registrar, has been assigned number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number P7298, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence under that number.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A few, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Re-examination by Mr. Stojanovic

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Andric, let us focus our attention to the part of the questions dealing with your statement provided to Mr. Ip in Tuzla and Sarajevo. Either/or; you were not sure yourself where it was. When passing through Konjevic Polje, did you at any point see any prisoners there?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at P7295. I think that's the number. Paragraph 8, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, there you say: "As we were approaching the cross-roads toward Konjevic Polje, I saw that Mladic stopped his vehicle approximately 100 metres before the cross-roads." Please tell us this: Do you recall stopping at the intersection itself in Konjevic Polje at any point in time en route to Zvornik or Milici and Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't remember having stopped at the intersection.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you. Now having seen the document, do you stand by your answer that at no point in time did you see Momir Nikolic along that road?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I stand by what I said, which is that I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you. The next thing. When the Prosecutor asked you about the Nikolic you mentioned whose first name you don't know but who was in your company in the Pinzgauer vehicle, accompanying you to Han Pijesak, having seen paragraph 20 of your statement, is it possible that Momir Nikolic was with you in the Pinzgauer vehicle at any point in time accompanying you to Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: No, that is not possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could we go to --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could we go to paragraph 20 of this document, which we have on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Can we have that? I didn't want to put leading questions, but it is P7295, paragraph 20 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I ask the witness at this point of time briefly. We discussed earlier the names contained in paragraph 20 and the last sentence reads: "However, it may include Bosko, perhaps Nikolic, and Nenad Djokic." Witness, can you tell me, is Bosko a first name or a family name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think Bosko is a first name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nikolic is a last name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And since this is your statement, is it possible that you referred to the person we have discussed earlier Bosko Nikolic? Or another Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I remember, there was no other Nikolic. When you showed me a moment ago the names of the members of the military police, the only possibility is this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, did you, at any point in time, have reason to doubt the words uttered by General Mladic when addressing the people at Sandici and Kasaba with regard to their transport to Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: That's what he said. It wasn't up to me to comment. I did not question it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Did General Mladic demand it of you as members of security to do anything that would be unlawful, inhumane, or unfair?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: No, did he not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: As you were leaving Vlasenica, to the best of your recollection, what time of day it may have been on the 13th of July? Could it have been evening?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Early evening, if I remember correctly. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, when did you pass through Konjevic Polje on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: On the way back?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: On your way to Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly. I think it was sometime in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: At that point in time, inside which vehicle was General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: It was a Puch jeep, a military vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Is it different in appearance from a passenger car, in terms of its technical ability?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Of course it's different.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic [as interpreted], you were asked today by the Prosecutor about events --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that you're not addressing Mr. Nikolic as is what appears in our interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour. I'd like to correct myself. Not Nikolic but Andric. I apologise if I said Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So, Mr. Andric, you answered the question who ordered you to go in front of the school in Bratunac, if you recalled. Please tell me this: Out of all the people who provided security, who did you see in front of the school; if you were able to recognise anyone, and if you remember?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know who you mean. The military policemen?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Were there any civilian policemen there?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: There were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Were there any locals, residents of Bratunac there?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Were there pleas made in terms of providing security for those people?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Were any comments made about it being an exceptionally dangerous situation for Bratunac town in terms of its security?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: That was a leading question that actually came at the conclusion of a series of leading questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic, you're constantly putting leading questions to the witness which are you supposed not to do. I'll address this matter in a second. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Mr. Andric, did you at any point in time that day observe anything in the conduct of General Mladic that would be unlawful?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I did not. He addressed the prisoners. Other than that, I didn't see anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Andric, for the answers you provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. I have a few questions. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the prisoners in Potocari, what could you tell about them? The prisoners on the 12th of July in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I can tell you it is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction I can tell you there were many women, children, men.

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: They appeared desperate and frightened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, let me interrupt you. I'm not talking about women, children, unless you considered them to have been prisoners at the time. But I was specifically ask you what you could tell us about the prisoners in Potocari on the 12th of July, such as where were they; do you know who had taken them prisoners; these kind of -- this kind of information.

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, they came there themselves to surrender. It was as a result of some talks. Nobody brought them there or forced them to come. They arrived on their own there, to the place of surrender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But even then, even then, what made them, as far as you understood the situation, what made them prisoners? If they voluntarily came, reported themselves, why were they prisoners?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: It is my opinion that they came there because the forces of the VRS had taken the town. As part of the talks, I think they went to the check-point of the UN.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Do you mean the Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The persons you described as prisoners.

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: They were not armed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were they in uniform?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Perhaps a few, but I don't remember exactly how many.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you now -- do you know why they had become prisoners?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: They became prisoners because -- well, I said so already. Because the army had taken that part of town and the agreement was that everyone goes there to surrender. That's how it was, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean including civilians?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And prisoners were taken from those who had surrendered, including civilians?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: It is not clear to me. What are you asking?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether those who had surrendered, which included, as you said, people in civilian clothing, without arms, that they were among those taken prisoner.

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: They came to that place. I don't know -- I don't know how to explain. From there, they were taken away on buses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you called them prisoners in your testimony.

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I used that term.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have another question for you. You were asked when you had left Vlasenica, whether that could have been in the evening hours. You remember that? And you said it may have been in the early evening. You remember that you told us that?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You also told us that you stopped in Vlasenica for lunch.

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the end of lunch-time, is that early evening?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Well, we couldn't decide when we would have lunch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, my question is whether you had lunch at a time that it was already early evening when you had finished your lunch. Or could it have been in the afternoon as well?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I think it was in the afternoon or in the evening, but I don't remember when precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions. Any further questions, Mr. Gillett? Judge Fluegge has one or more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In which capacity have you been at these locations on the 11th, 12th, and 13th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: As a military policeman. Providing security for General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Up to which point have you been member of the military police platoon?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't recall the exact date. Perhaps until the 15th or 16th. Maybe up to the 20th. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which month?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That would mean that during that time-period, mid-July, you were no longer member of the military police; correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What is true? Were you member of the military police mid-July or not?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: As I said, it was the 20th at the latest of June. So May, June, July, August, if I know the sequence of months well enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You said you were in your capacity as a military police platoon member present in these locations mid-July. Now you again and again say you stopped your term of office in the military police already in June. I don't understand that, but I can leave it to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I may be able to quickly try and assist with that question. Very quickly. If we could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could keep in mind that we are already beyond 2.15, and we would all try to avoid that the witness has to stay here for another four or five days until we can finish with the last 5 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Absolutely. If we could get 65 ter document 32387 on the monitor. And if we could go to page 3 of this. Further cross-examination by Mr. Gillett:

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And, sir, this is another statement that gave to local authorities in Bosnia. And if we look at paragraph 3, it says: "I became a military policeman of the Bratunac Brigade in 1994, and I left on 15, 16, or 17 July 1995. I don't recall when exactly." Does that refresh your recollection that it was mid-July when you left the Bratunac Brigade military police?

utterances.speaker: PERO ANDRIC
utterances.text: I think that what I stated then was 100 per cent wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, this concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you, put to you by the parties, put to you by the Bench. I wish you a safe return home again and you may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, before we adjourn, as I said before, I briefly address the matter of leading questions. I read one of your questions put to the witness: "As you were leaving Vlasenica, to the best of your recollection, what time of the day it may have been on the 13th of July? Could it have been evening? " Which is as leading can be. Never heard a more clear example of a leading question. And then, of course, the witness followed your suggestion and said: "Early evening, if I remember correctly." And then I asked again about lunch time about -- and then he said: "I don't know," as a matter of fact. Mr. Stojanovic, by using these leading questions, you are -- you take a risk of diminishing the probative value of the testimony of the witness you called. So when earlier you just seemed to be not very impressed by objections against leading questions, I give you this one simple example and I would advise you to think it over more thoroughly and perhaps to take the rule that in examination-in-chief you shouldn't lead the witness more seriously. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I promised you a responses to your earlier inquiry about the videolink motion. The Prosecution has no objection. And if I may take just 60 more seconds, I would also mention that during the course of Witness Erceg's cross-examination, the Prosecution used 65 ter 02780 and 18494, two documents which had inadvertently been omitted from the list of exhibits. Thereafter, a discussion ensued between the Prosecution and Defence. Mr. Traldi didn't immediately tender those for that reason. And the Defence expressed no objection to their tendering. So we can either formally tender them at the beginning of the court session on Tuesday or we do so now, as the Court wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I'd prefer to do it on Tuesday because we're already so far beyond the court time, and of course we did it because the Easter weekend is coming up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, I didn't even ask permission to continue to the booth assisting us. That's a failure. I should have done that. But it's nevertheless highly appreciated that you made it possible for us to conclude the testimony of this witness before the weekend. I do understand, by the way, by a gesture of Mr. Mladic that he would like to consult most likely with Mr. Stojanovic. It should be done very quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently nothing to be raised. Consultation perhaps should have taken place outside the courtroom after we had adjourned. We adjourn and resume on Tuesday, the 7th of April, Courtroom I, 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
